public_body: Cotuit Fire District Policy Advisory Committee
overall: The AG found the Fire District Policy Advisory Committee, which had wrongly believed it was not a public body, violated G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a) by failing to keep sufficient minutes for eight meetings; it ordered complete minutes created within 60 days and only reminded the committee on the notice and complaint-response issues.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to maintain minutes for eight meetings between November 2010 and May 2011; the chair gave handwritten notes instead.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee failed to create and approve complete minutes for the eight meetings at issue.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that topics discussed at the May 10, 2011 meeting (union decertification, a bylaw on Fire Department raises) were not listed in the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: We also remind the Committee that meeting notices must state the "date, time and place of such meeting and a listing of topics that the chair reasonably anticipates will be discussed at the meeting."

allegations.summary: The committee took 43 business days to respond to the complaint filed in August 2011, and the AG had received only an extension request without a stated reason.
allegations.key_passage: Because it is a public body, the Committee was required to send a copy of the complaint to the Attorney General and notify the Attorney General of any remedial action taken within 14 business days of receipt.

remedy: Within sixty (60) days of receipt of the letter, create and approve complete and accurate minutes of the eight meetings requested by the complainant, to the best of its ability.
remedy_passage: Furthermore, we order the ComiMttee, to the best of its ability, to create and approve complete and accurate minutes of the eight meetings requested by the complainant.
